initial_plan.answerability: yes: the dataset has yearly crash fatality counts for motorists and cyclists, though it cannot establish exposure-adjusted risk or explain causes
initial_plan.metric: annual number of motorist deaths and annual number of cyclist deaths, each summed across crash rows
initial_plan.population: police-reported NYC crash rows dated from 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31; death counts classify fatalities as motorists or cyclists

data_check_interpretation: The selected 2013-2025 population contains 2,132,218 crash rows, with 85,546 to 231,564 rows per year. Every year has observed dates from January 1 through December 31, though the file alone cannot verify complete reporting. No selected crash_date values or summed death fields are missing; crash_date is DATE typed, so invalid string encodings are not possible, and no sentinel date is specified. No rows need to be excluded or counted differently; retain all crash rows in the selected years.

final_plan.answerability: yes for comparing the recorded annual counts of motorist and cyclist deaths; the data do not support exposure-adjusted risk or explanations for changes
final_plan.metric: annual sum of number_of_motorist_killed and annual sum of number_of_cyclist_killed, reported as separate raw counts
final_plan.population: all police-reported NYC crash rows with crash_date from 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31, including rows with zero deaths
final_plan.missing_value_decision: retain all selected rows; the data check found no missing values in either summed death column
final_plan.limitations: The file spans January 1 through December 31 in each year, but that does not prove complete reporting. Counts are police-reported deaths in two categories, not exposure-adjusted risk, and do not explain causes or include pedestrian deaths in either series.
